page: Amazon Web Services i8ge.metal-48xl is a storage-optimized bare-metal server powered by AWS Graviton processors. It features 192 dedicated physical cores built on the ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 2.7 GHz. The system is equipped with 1536.0 GB of DDR5 memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance includes 120,000 GB of NVMe SSD capacity. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 300 Gbps.

Benchmark results show top-tier multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core CPU scoring 287,164.37 and Geekbench multi-core reaching 20,677.0. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, achieving 13,947.51 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 897.06 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Database and caching operations are exceptionally strong, as evidenced by a Passmark database score of 46,115.93 and Redis SET operations reaching 378.59 million operations per second. However, single-core performance is moderate, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1,666.0, and LLM text generation is poor, registering only 28.16 tokens per second on a small model.

The bare-metal architecture and high density of NVMe storage make this server highly cost-efficient for workloads requiring massive local storage and high-throughput memory access without hypervisor overhead. The 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and 120 TB of local NVMe SSD storage position this instance for large-scale database deployments, high-performance caching layers, big data analytics, and intensive multi-threaded processing tasks such as software compilation and ray tracing.
